newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK GOVT SEES 98 BUDGET WITH SKK 35 BLN DEFICIT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK GOVT SEES 98 BUDGET WITH SKK 35 BLN DEFICIT.

text.p: The Slovak government on Tuesday approved the basic principles for the 1998 state budget projecting a deficit of about 35 billion crowns.

The draft, which will now be returned to ministries for further consultation before it is presented to parliament, is based on real gross domestic product (GDP) growth of at least five percent and an annual inflation rate of around six percent by the end of 1998.

"The budget projection estimates revenues at 175 billion crowns...this should be considered as critical and revenues should not be lower," said the document presented by the Finance Ministry. Expenditures are projected to total around 210 billion crowns.
Debt servicing should total some 40 billion crowns in 1998, including paying off state bonds issued in 1997. Some 28.5 billion crowns should go to paying the actual state debt.
The 1997 state budget plans a deficit of 36.9 billion crowns on revenues of 171.1 billion crowns and expenditures at 208.0 billion crowns.

Maria Suranova, head of the finance ministry's state budget department, told Reuters the ministry should present the first draft law on the state budget back to the government after the consultations by mid-September.
According to law, the government must present the budget to parliament for final approval by November 15.
Slovak GDP rose by 6.9 percent, year-on-year, in 1996 and is forecast to slow-down to 5.6 percent in 1997.

Consumer inflation stood at 0.1 percent month-on-month in May, putting prices 6.1 percent higher than in the same month in 1996. The annual inflation rate is forecast at between 6.4-6.7 percent by the end of 1997.
